summary.en: Dragging to a secondary screen is reported to prevent the next drag. A display-specific report, not proof of the single-screen failure.
A second monitor report records negative window coordinates. GitHub marks it closed/completed; that state alone does not establish a released fix.
Opening the overlay reportedly coincides with task-switching stalls and unresponsive dragging. Its broader performance symptoms may have a different cause.
The activity badge reportedly stops accepting input after moving to the lower-right corner. The badge is overlay UI, not the pet artwork.
A July report describes the usable input area shrinking away from the visible pet over time, affecting both built-in and custom pets. This is the counter's anchor.
A single-display regression report covers built-in and custom pets. A community comment redirects discussion to #34227; this is not an official duplicate decision.
The reporter ties an undersized input area to selecting a custom pet at the first wake. The reported built-in-first workaround should not be generalized to all reports.
A report after update 26.825.31414 includes frozen animation as well as failed interaction. It is broader than a click-through-only report.
Reselecting or refreshing the pet reportedly permits exactly one reposition before dragging stops again.
Built-in and custom pets reportedly pass clicks to the window behind them. Its discussion connects several reports; this editorial hub is not an official master issue.
The transparent overlay reportedly blocks clicks over a large area while the pet remains unusable. This is the opposite input-routing outcome to click-through.
The reporter describes a visible floating pet whose clicks reach the application behind it, despite resets and switching built-in pets.
This report isolates input loss after the first drag while animation continues, across built-in and custom pets in a multi-monitor setup.
Hover responses continue but clicks and dragging fail. The issue is closed/completed; the bot's suggestion of #41465 does not establish a fix or official duplicate decision.
A validated custom pet reportedly cannot receive input and may disappear after switching. The reporter's local workaround is not a shipped fix.
This report describes partial or complete click-through at 150% display scaling and explicitly points to #34227.

Editorial comparison: both describe visible pets failing to receive input, with different onset and extent. Similarity does not establish a common bug.
Editorial comparison: both describe a successful first move followed by lost interaction. Their environments and diagnostic detail differ.
Weak editorial connection: both involve the Windows pet overlay and impaired mouse interaction. The stall report may be a separate performance failure.
Unconfirmed hypothesis: stale region measurements might connect initialization and later drift. No shared root cause is asserted.
Unconfirmed hypothesis: region synchronization after moving the overlay might connect first-drag failure and click-through. Community analysis is not an official diagnosis.
Opposite observed outcomes: clicks escape the pet in one report and are swallowed by transparent space in the other. A shared mechanism remains unconfirmed.
